name: @thetis/tool-exec
description: Tools for the model: install, fork, remove, delete and configure packages, spawn subagents in your own space, and read your other conversations. Running commands is @thetis/terminal.

thetis.label: extensions, helper chats and past conversations
thetis.summary: Lets your assistant install and set up extensions for you, hand work to helper chats, and look back through your other conversations.

tools.name: list_packages
tools.description: List the packages installed in your userspace: each one's name, version, type and description, the steps and tools it declares, its bench suites, and what it was forked from. The system prompt does not carry this list; call this when you need to know what is installed or which package provides a tool or step.

type.description: Only packages of this type, such as tool, loader, provider, skill or service

tools.name: install_package
tools.description: Install a package into your userspace from a directory path (relative to home) or a git URL. The package must have a package.json with a thetis field and be scoped @<you>/<name>. It takes effect when this reply ends.

tools.name: uninstall_package
tools.description: Remove an installed package from your userspace by name. Its files stay. When it was a fork that replaced another package, that package comes back.

tools.name: fork_package
tools.description: Copy an installed package into packages/<as> under your home as @<you>/<as>, ready to edit and then install_package. Installing the fork replaces the original; uninstalling the fork puts the original back. Does not install.

name.description: The installed package to copy, such as @thetis/tools-plan

as.description: The directory name under packages/; default is the unscoped name

tools.name: unfork_package
tools.description: The inverse of fork_package: uninstall a fork and put the package it was copied from back in its place, with every change that package has had since. The fork's files under packages/ are kept unless deleteFiles says otherwise. Refuses when the original is not on disk here, so it is safe to run on a forked gateway.

deleteFiles.description: Delete the fork's directory under packages/ as well. Default false: the files are kept.

tools.name: delete_package
tools.description: Uninstall a package in your own scope and delete its directory under packages/ in your home. When it was a fork, the original comes back. Refuses @thetis/* packages.

tools.name: package_config
tools.description: Show what a package installed in your userspace is configured with: every key's state (set, missing or unset), which layer the value comes from and whether a fork inherits it, the value of a non-secret key, and the help of each declared key. A secret is shown as ••• and never its value.

tools.name: configure_package
tools.description: Set or unset one configuration key of an installed package in the person's own layer. Prefer asking the person to set a secret in the panel: a secret pasted into the conversation stays in the transcript. A key declared for the system is set by an admin in the panel, not here. The change is live on the next call. A string value may hold ${VAR} to read a variable from the environment; pass json: true to send a number, boolean, object or array. The reply names the key and its new state, never the value.

key.description: The key, as package_config lists it

value.description: The value to store; required unless unset is true

unset.description: Remove the key from the person's layer instead of setting it

json.description: Parse value as JSON before storing it

tools.name: spawn_subagent
tools.description: Start a subagent session in your userspace (same files and packages), send it a task, and return its final reply. It runs on this conversation's model unless `model` names another. Several spawn_subagent calls in one reply run at the same time. The person watches the subagent work under its label. The first line of the result names it: [subagent <id> <label>]. Stopping your turn stops the subagent. A subagent may spawn subagents of its own. When a subagent fails part-way and the result says it can be continued, use resume_subagent rather than spawning a new one.

label.description: A short name for the subagent, shown to the person, for example research.

model.description: A model id for the subagent, when the task wants a different one than this conversation's. Leave it out to use this conversation's model.

tools.name: resume_subagent
tools.description: Continue a subagent of this conversation from where its last turn stopped, for example after a dropped connection or a restart. Nothing it finished is done again and no message is added. The result has the same shape as spawn_subagent's. A subagent that had already finished answers with its last reply.

id.description: The subagent's session id, from the first line of its result: [subagent <id> ...]

label.description: The short name it was given, so the result line names it the same way.

model.description: A model id for the continued turn. Leave it out to use this conversation's model.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List the person's conversations, newest first: id, last update, name, turns, running/interrupted/archived, subagents, first and last message. Subagents only when asked for.

query.description: Text in the name, first or last message.

tools.name: read_conversation
tools.description: Read another of the person's conversations as numbered messages, the newest by default, with brief tool calls. A running one shows its reply so far.

offset.description: 1-based first message; negative counts from the end.

tools.name: search_conversations
tools.description: Regex search over the person's other conversations, newest first; hits grouped by conversation with message number and context. Searches user and assistant text unless roles adds tool. Says when it stopped early.

pattern.description: JavaScript regex, case-insensitive unless ignore_case is false.

tools.name: summarize_conversation
tools.description: Summarize another of the person's conversations: the ask, what was done, where it ended. One model request with no tools, on this conversation's model unless model is given; it costs that request and changes nothing.
